method.title: How these numbers are made
method.source: Source. FIO, the community service fed by players' game clients, through PRUNplanner's public game data. Daily prices cover full UTC days; order books are current.
method.turnover: Turnover is traded quantity × price, summed over AI1, CI1, IC1 and NC1. Each exchange has its own currency (AIC, CIS, ICA, NCC). The same material trades at close to the same price everywhere, so sums treat the currencies at par. Every filled trade counts once, whether a seller filled a bid or a buyer filled an ask. Trades with market makers count too. Orders that aren't filled don't count, and the data doesn't say which side started a trade.
method.prices: Prices are VWAP 7D and VWAP 30D only: turnover ÷ units over the window, so thin days barely count. A chart point is the VWAP 7D on that day.
method.index: Index. Every material with a VWAP 7D on each day of the 90. Weight = 30-day turnover share, capped at 5 % (20 % within a sector), the rest spread over the others.
method.movers: Movers compare VWAP 7D with VWAP 30D, like the Trend in Market Exploration. The 30 days include the last 7, so changes look smaller than week on week.
method.gaps: Price gaps. Last 7 days compares each exchange's VWAP 7D, so a gap there may already be gone; Books now checks the best ask on the cheaper exchange against the best bid on the dearer one. Order books now uses only those top prices, not how much is on offer. Neither counts shipping, fuel or flight time.
method.heavy_day: One heavy day shows for a week. A single large trade at an unusual price pulls the VWAP 7D for as long as it sits in the 7-day window, then the price snaps back.
method.not_included: Not in here: local markets, contracts and trades inside corporations. They never touch the exchanges, so this is the CX, not the whole economy.
method.flat: Flat marks materials whose daily VWAP stays within ±0.3 % of its 30-day median on at least 80 % of trading days, usually because market makers buy or sell them at fixed prices. They count in turnover but are left out of the movers and the price gaps.
